items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 60:1
items.html: The extra Hey of the sixth day alludes to the fifth Hesed that is completed at that hour: for the sixth day is the discernment of Yesod, which includes the five Hassadim and the five Gevurot. Until midday enter the five Hassadim and that which includes them, and from midday onward enter the five Gevurot and that which includes them. Thus, at the fifth hour the fifth Hesed enters, and it is found that all six days were completed in the discernment of the Hassadim, which are the main thing, since nothing is lacking until the completion, except the five Gevurot after midday, which are not so essential, because they receive from the five Hassadim. Therefore the entry of the fifth Hesed is considered the completion and conclusion of the six days of creation, and the beginning of the illumination of the day of Shabbat. Hence the worlds begin then to ascend with the ascents of Shabbat. And to this alludes the extra Hey of the sixth day. (Item 77).
